value.name: California SGIP - current category and budget check required
value.description: New applications and waitlist applications for ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets closed on December 30, 2025. New AB 209 applications have a June 30, 2028 deadline. The 2026 SGIP rate table publishes $3.10/W for solar and $1.10/Wh for storage in applicable Residential Solar and Storage Equity categories. Household eligibility and live budget availability vary by category and program administrator; check the official Program Metrics tracker before relying on an incentive.
value.eligibility: Eligibility varies by 2026 SGIP budget category, program administrator, property, income/pathway, project rules, and live funding availability.

battery_programs.notes: SGIP program data refreshed on 2026-08-26 from the official 2026 Handbook and live Program Metrics. Earlier locality records contained 2025 opening/availability language. This record does not assert household eligibility, reservation availability, or a guaranteed incentive; current category and program-administrator status must be checked before reliance.

value: Log in to or create an account in the City's OpenGov online permitting system
For a permit originally issued in eTRAKiT, select the issuing department, submit the 'Inspection Request (Permits Issued in eTRAKiT)' record, then use '+ New Appointment' to request the inspection
For a permit issued in OpenGov, open the permit record's Inspections tab and use '+ New Appointment'
City staff will schedule the inspection and send an email notification
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building/Fire inspection scheduling process via its OpenGov permitting system (the same process covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not describe a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence.

value.program_or_pathway: Standard residential solar permit (OpenGov online permitting system)
other_conditions: Solar panels, battery backup, and/or service panel upgrades done simultaneously can be included on a single solar permit (additional fees may apply)
Reroof-with-solar-tile permits should list only the reroof value, excluding solar tile costs
Building permits issued after January 1, 2023 are valid for 2 years; minor permits expire after 180 days
All new permit applications must be submitted through OpenGov beginning February 23, 2026
